title: Spark runs one MainnetController and replicates a ForeignController on every other chain
content:
The ALM contract listings in A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.1.1.1.2 name two controller implementations. Ethereum Mainnet runs `ALM_CONTROLLER (MainnetController)` at version 1.10; every other chain — Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism, Avalanche, Robinhood Chain, X Layer — runs `ALM_CONTROLLER (ForeignController)`, and each chain additionally has its own ALM_PROXY and ALM_RATE_LIMITS contracts.

The asymmetry encodes where authority lives. Ethereum is where USDS is issued and where the Allocator Vault sits, so the home controller can do things a remote one cannot — mint against the vault, interact directly with Sky's core. Foreign controllers operate on tokens that have already arrived, within limits set from home.

Using a single ForeignController implementation across seven chains is the other half of the choice. One audited contract replicated per chain means a new chain is a deployment rather than a design exercise, and a fix or upgrade applies to a known set of identical deployments. That is what makes the observed expansion rate — including chains as unusual as Robinhood Chain and X Layer — operationally plausible.

The concentration risk is the flip side: a defect in ForeignController is a defect on every non-Ethereum chain simultaneously, which is why per-chain rate limits and freeze capability are configured separately even though the controller code is shared.
description: The ALM contract set is deliberately asymmetric: Ethereum hosts the distinct home-chain controller while Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism, Avalanche, Robinhood Chain and X Layer share one
